column1: # boru Language Specification: the boru:emitlang module + the core `emit` word
# `emit <kind> <opts?> <data>` is the symmetric inverse of `parse`: it expands
# at the call site to the STANDARD emitter call
# `EmitLang get emit_<kind> <data> <opts> end`. The `data` is the REQUIRED LAST
# surface arg and `opts` is the optional MIDDLE one — disambiguated by arity.
# The kind is OPTIONAL: bare `emit <data>` routes to emit_auto, which picks the
# value's natural format (Map/List/scalar/Error → json, Table → csv, Xml → xml).
# Every emitter traverses the value through the canonical walk engine — one code
# path for all formats. The kind set is FIXED (`EmitLang.kinds` lists it;
# `EmitLang.register` is a tombstone raising emit_registry_frozen) — custom
# emitters are Function VALUES (`emit <fn> <data>`, §fnv). A shape a format
# cannot represent raises emit_unsupported; an unknown explicit kind raises
# (Emit results are Strings, so the canonical expected form is single-quoted.)
# §1  emit — auto (natural format) and explicit json

column1: # §fnv  an emitter VALUE as the target — `emit <fn> <opts?> <data>`. The
#       first operand may BE the emitter: a Function (or a word bound to one)
#       whose every signature is [value:Any opts:Map …] → [String …] — the
#       shared EmitLangFnSigWhy validator (the same prefix the built-in kinds
#       carry). A built-in kind wins a name collision; without these forms a
#       Function operand would fall to emit_auto and JSON-emit the fn value.
import "boru:emitlang"  def up fn [[value:Any opts:Map] [String] ['UP']]  emit up {a:1}
column3: a word bound to an emitter fn is the value form spelled by name
